children: fell 5% in Thursday's trading as Argus downgraded shares to Hold from Buy, as aluminum prices remain near multi-month lows as supply improves outside the Middle East.
is having trouble overcoming the pricing pressures, prompting Argus analyst Alexandra Yates to reduce her rating until seeing more of a rebound in the market driven by long-term sustainable demand.
Yates also said she is concerned about market volatility, as Alcoa
is heavily exposed to the global market and faces potential downside from expanding supplies and investment in production capacity by competitors.
Unfavorable tariff conditions and expanding capacity from international competitors continue to create headwinds that impede a sustainable commodity market recovery, the analyst said.
Despite near-term industry challenges, Yates raised her FY 2026 adjusted earnings estimate for Alcoa
to $6.80/share from $6.55 and maintained the FY 2027 forecast at $6.70/share, saying the shares appear fairly valued near recent prices at ~$41, trading at 6x forward earnings projections.

title: Alcoa downgraded at Argus as near-term margins hit by mounting pricing pressures
